mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher consumer spending and increased demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of strong GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 1.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when the federal funds rate exceeds 1.5%, or the federal funds rate does not significantly predict S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 8% indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when the unemployment rate exceeds 8%, or the unemployment rate does not significantly predict S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts and GDP are increasing, it indicates a strong and growing economy, leading to increased demand for goods and services, and ultimately resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when both housing starts and GDP are increasing, or the joint effect of housing starts and GDP on S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates an increase in the supply of goods and services, leading to increased economic activity and ultimately resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when industrial production is increasing, or industrial production does not significantly predict S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and the CPI is increasing, it indicates an expansionary monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, and ultimately resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative when the federal funds rate is below 1% and the CPI is increasing, or the joint effect of the federal funds rate and CPI on S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 5% indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and ultimately resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when the unemployment rate is below 5%, or the unemployment rate does not significantly predict S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both retail sales and GDP are decreasing, it indicates a weakening economy, leading to decreased demand for goods and services, and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when both retail sales and GDP are decreasing, or the joint effect of retail sales and GDP on S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).
